text: Correctly stated: the complement in ℂ of any subset homeomorphic to the circle has exactly two connected components, the Jordan curve theorem (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cor. 2B.2; Munkres, *Topology*, §§61–63); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the diagonals (Re⟪T eₖ, eₖ⟫)ₖ of a symmetric operator T on an n-dimensional real or complex inner product space, over its orthonormal bases, are exactly the convex hull of the rearrangements of its eigenvalues, the Schur–Horn theorem in both directions (Horn, Amer. J. Math. 76 (1954); Marshall–Olkin–Arnold, Thm 9.B.1–9.B.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the Lazard ring, the universal ring of one-dimensional commutative formal group laws, is isomorphic as a ℤ-algebra to the polynomial ring ℤ[x₁, x₂, …] by evaluation at its generators xₙ, Lazard's theorem (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism*, Thm A2.1.8; Adams, *Stable Homotopy and Generalised Homology*, Part II §7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: over a finite-dimensional algebra A over a field, every finitely generated indecomposable non-projective A-module M ends an almost split sequence 0 → τM → E → M → 0 with E finitely generated and τ the Auslander–Reiten translate, the existence half of the Auslander–Reiten theorem (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, Thm V.1.15; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Thm IV.3.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: if F ∈ ℤ[X₀, X₁] is a binary form such that F(X, 1) has at least three distinct complex roots and m ≠ 0, the Thue equation F(x, y) = m has only finitely many integer solutions, Thue's theorem (Thue 1909; Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation* lecture notes, Cor. 6.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: every m × n integer matrix A has U ∈ GL_n(ℤ) and H in column-style Hermite normal form with A·U = [H | 0], existence of the Hermite normal form (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, Thm 2.4.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: two integer matrices of the same size in column-style upper Hermite normal form with the same column lattice are equal, uniqueness of the Hermite normal form (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, Thm 2.4.3, §2.4.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for an invertible real square matrix A indexed by a nonempty finite type and bounds aᵢ ≥ 0 with |det A| ≤ ∏ aᵢ, some nonzero integer vector z has |∑ⱼ Aᵢⱼ zⱼ| ≤ aᵢ for every i, Minkowski's linear forms theorem in its non-strict form (Cassels, *Geometry of Numbers*, III Thm III; Hardy–Wright, Thm 448); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a convex subset of the dual of a Banach space over ℝ or ℂ is weak-star closed if and only if its intersection with every closed ball about 0 is weak-star closed, the Krein–Šmulian theorem (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*, Thm V.12.1; Megginson, Thm 2.7.11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: if a group G with a Tits system (BN-pair) with at least one simple reflection and irreducible Weyl group is perfect and is the normal closure of a solvable subgroup normalized by B, then G modulo the normal core of B is simple, Tits's simplicity theorem (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, Ch. IV §2 no. 7, Thm 5; Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §29.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a discrete group G is amenable (has a left-invariant mean on bounded functions) if and only if for every finite K ⊆ G and ε > 0 some finite nonempty F has |gF △ F| < ε|F| for all g ∈ K, Følner's theorem (Følner 1955; Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, *Kazhdan's Property (T)*, Thms G.3.1 and G.5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a discrete group is amenable (has a left-invariant mean on bounded functions) if and only if it has Følner sets, that is Mathlib's Følner filter for the counting measure is nontrivial, Følner's theorem (Følner 1955; Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, *Kazhdan's Property (T)*, Thms G.3.1 and G.5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for arc bounds lo ≤ hi in a linearly ordered abelian group on a finite quiver, a circulation f with lo ≤ f ≤ hi exists if and only if, for every vertex set S, the lower bounds on the arcs entering S total at most the upper bounds on the arcs leaving S, Hoffman's circulation theorem (Hoffman 1960; Schrijver, *Combinatorial Optimization*, Thm 11.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: every rational representation of GL_n(ℂ), one whose matrix entries are polynomials in the entries of g divided by a power of det g, is completely reducible, by Weyl's unitarian trick (Weyl, *The Classical Groups*, Ch. VIII §11; Goodman–Wallach, §2.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for 𝕜 = ℝ or ℂ, a subgroup of GL_n(𝕜) is maximal among the compact subgroups if and only if it is a conjugate of the unitary subgroup, O(n) over ℝ and U(n) over ℂ (Knapp, *Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction*, Ch. VI; Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, §2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: multiplication (k, a, u) ↦ kau is a homeomorphism from O(n) × (positive diagonal matrices) × (upper unitriangular matrices) onto GL_n(ℝ), the Iwasawa decomposition of GL_n(ℝ) as a homeomorphism, where Knapp states a diffeomorphism (Knapp, *Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction*, §VI.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: every invertible real n × n matrix factors uniquely as k·a·u with k orthogonal, a diagonal with positive entries and u upper unitriangular, the Iwasawa decomposition of GL_n(ℝ) (Knapp, *Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction*, §VI.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for 𝕜 = ℝ or ℂ, every A ∈ GL_n(𝕜) is uniquely a product PU of a positive definite matrix P and a unitary matrix U, orthogonal over ℝ, the polar decomposition of an invertible matrix (Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, §2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: over any commutative ring, a set G of multivariate polynomials whose nonzero members have unit leading coefficients is a Gröbner basis of the ideal it generates if and only if 0 is a remainder of every S-polynomial of two members of G on division by G, Buchberger's criterion (Cox–Little–O'Shea, *Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms*, Ch. 2 §6, Thm 6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for any monomial order, every ideal of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a Noetherian ring has a finite Gröbner basis (Cox–Little–O'Shea, *Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms*, Ch. 2 §5, Cor. 6, over a field); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for k ≥ 2, a sequence a : ℕ → Δ is k-automatic if and only if its k-kernel {n ↦ a(kᵉn + r) : r < kᵉ} is finite, Eilenberg's theorem, with automata reading the base-k digits least significant first (Allouche–Shallit, *Automatic Sequences*, Thm 6.6.2; Bridy, Thm 2.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for every permutation σ of {1, …, n}, the Robinson–Schensted correspondence of σ⁻¹ is that of σ with the insertion and recording tableaux exchanged, Schützenberger's symmetry theorem (Stanley, EC2, Thm 7.13.1; Schützenberger 1963); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a hyperbolic triple p, q, r of elliptic orders or cusps (1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1), some hyperbolic triangle has angles π/p, π/q, π/r, and its triangle group, generated by products of reflections in its sides, is a cofinite Fuchsian group isomorphic to the abstract triangle group ⟨x, y, z | x^p, y^q, z^r, zyx⟩ (Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §10.6; Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, §4.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: if a side pairing of a convex hyperbolic polygon with finite or ideal vertices satisfies the angle condition at every finite vertex cycle and has parabolic cycle transformations at the ideal vertices, the group generated by the side-pairing maps is a cofinite Fuchsian group, as Poincaré's polygon theorem states (Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §9.8; Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, §4.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a discrete subgroup Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ) is cofinite if and only if its Dirichlet domain centred at a point with trivial stabilizer is a convex polygon with finitely many vertices, possibly ideal, Siegel's theorem with its Gauss–Bonnet converse (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Thm 4.1.1; Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §10.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a cofinite Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ) and a centre with trivial stabilizer, the Dirichlet domain is a convex polygon with finitely many vertices and a side pairing by elements of Γ, and Γ is presented by the side-pairing maps subject to the side relations and the finite-vertex cycle relations, the converse of Poincaré's polygon theorem (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, §4.3; Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §9.8); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for primitive binary quadratic forms f, g of the same nonsquare discriminant D, not only D < 0, there are united representatives (a, B, a'C) and (a', B, aC) of their classes, and the Picard class of their Dirichlet composition (aa', B, C) is the product of the classes of f and g; the rest of Cox's Thm 3.9 is in other declarations (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Lemma 3.2, Thm 3.9); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a finite abelian extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, the Artin conductor exponents of the characters of Gal(L/K), with values in a commutative monoid with enough roots of unity such as ℂ, sum to the discriminant exponent v_K(𝔡_{L/K}), the local conductor–discriminant formula in its abelian form (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, Ch. VI §3; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VII §11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a reflexive positive definite bilinear form on a ℤ-module M, a set of submodules is the set of orthogonal components exactly when its members are orthogonally indecomposable, pairwise orthogonal and span M, so such a decomposition exists and is unique, Eichler's theorem (Eichler, Math. Ann. 125 (1952); O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 105:1; Milnor–Husemoller, *Symmetric Bilinear Forms*, II Thm 6.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: every unbounded cochain complex of left modules over any ring admits a quasi-isomorphism into a K-injective complex, Spaltenstein's theorem for modules (Spaltenstein, *Resolutions of unbounded complexes*, Compositio Math. 65 (1988); Stacks Project, Tag 079P); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: over a commutative ring, every flat module is the filtered colimit of the finite free modules mapping to it, with the canonical cocone as colimit: the direction flat ⇒ filtered colimit of finite free modules of Lazard's theorem; the converse is not stated (Lazard 1969; Stacks Project, Tag 058G); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a function from a finite-dimensional real inner product space to a finite-dimensional real normed space that is harmonic at a point is real analytic there (Evans, PDE, §2.2.3, Thm 10; Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, *Harmonic Function Theory*, Thm 1.28); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for 1 < p < ∞, an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, a compact K ⊆ Ω and coefficients aᵢⱼ measurable on Ω and continuous and elliptic at each point of K, every u ∈ W^{2,p}(Ω) with ∑ aᵢⱼ ∂ᵢ∂ⱼu = f ∈ Lᵖ(Ω) satisfies ‖D²u‖_{Lᵖ(K)} ≤ C(‖f‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} + ‖u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)}), the interior Calderón–Zygmund estimate for the principal part only, without lower-order terms, bounding D²u rather than the whole W^{2,p} norm, and with u taken in W^{2,p}(Ω) rather than W^{2,p}_loc ∩ Lᵖ (Gilbarg–Trudinger, *Elliptic PDE of Second Order*, Thm 9.11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a convex body K of positive volume in a Euclidean space of dimension n ≥ 1 satisfies P(K)ⁿ ≥ nⁿ ω_n |K|ⁿ⁻¹, P the De Giorgi perimeter and ω_n the volume of the unit ball, the isoperimetric inequality for convex bodies, not for all sets of finite perimeter (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, §7.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for any group action, if each of A and B is equidecomposable, with finitely many pieces, with a subset of the other, then A and B are equidecomposable, the Banach–Schröder–Bernstein theorem (Tomkowicz–Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Ch. 3, Thm 3.6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, if the characteristic functions of a sequence of probability measures converge pointwise to a function f continuous at 0, there is a unique probability measure with characteristic function f and the sequence converges weakly to it, Lévy's continuity theorem with existence (Billingsley, *Probability and Measure*, §26, Thm 26.3, and §29); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a p × n integer matrix A with linearly independent rows and p < n, Ax = 0 has a nonzero integer solution with sup norm at most (√det(AAᵀ)/g)^{1/(n−p)}, g the gcd of the maximal minors, Siegel's lemma in Bombieri–Vaaler's form (Bombieri–Vaaler, *On Siegel's lemma*, Invent. Math. 73 (1983), Thm 1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for distinct nonadjacent vertices s, t of a finite simple graph, there are k internally disjoint s–t paths and k vertices other than s and t whose deletion separates s from t, which with weak duality is Menger's theorem: the greatest number of such paths equals the least size of such a separator (Diestel, *Graph Theory*, Thm 3.3.1; Menger 1927); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for arc bounds lo ≤ hi and vertex bounds a ≤ b in a linearly ordered abelian group, an assignment within the arc bounds whose excess at each vertex lies between a and b exists if and only if a(S) ≤ U(Sᶜ) and −U(S) ≤ b(S) for every vertex set S, where U(S) = hi(δ⁺S) − lo(δ⁻S), the interval form of Gale's supply–demand feasibility theorem (Gale, *A theorem on flows in networks*, 1957; Ford–Fulkerson, *Flows in Networks*, §II.1; Schrijver, *Combinatorial Optimization*, §11.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: over any ring A, possibly noncommutative, for u ∈ GL_m(A) the block diagonal matrix u ⊕ u⁻¹ lies in the elementary subgroup of GL_{2m}(A), generated by the transvections, Whitehead's lemma (Milnor, *Introduction to Algebraic K-Theory*, Lemma 3.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form over an algebraically closed field, every x is n + s with [n, s] = 0, ad n nilpotent, ad s semisimple, and both polynomials in ad x, the existence of the abstract Jordan decomposition (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §5.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for an orthonormal basis b of a real or complex inner product space and any family v, the determinant of v in the coordinates of b has norm at most ∏ ‖vᵢ‖, Hadamard's inequality (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, Thm 7.8.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for every level N ≥ 1 and weight k ≥ 3, the normalized Eisenstein series E_k^{ψ,φ,t} span the Eisenstein subspace of M_k(Γ₁(N)), the complement of the cusp forms (Diamond–Shurman, *A First Course in Modular Forms*, Thm 4.5.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for a Coxeter system of type A_{n−1} on W, the elements T_w (w ∈ W) form a basis of the type-A Iwahori–Hecke algebra over every commutative ring and every unit q, the basis theorem, for the type-A algebra only (Iwahori 1964; Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §7.1; Mathas, *Iwahori–Hecke algebras and Schur algebras of the symmetric group*, Thm 1.13); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for Coxeter systems on W and W' and a map f of their index sets along which the Coxeter matrices agree, the induced homomorphism W → W' is injective, the injectivity in the theorem that standard parabolic subgroups of Coxeter groups are Coxeter groups (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, Ch. IV §1 no. 8, Thm 2; Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §5.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: between finite-dimensional real symplectic vector spaces of the same dimension, an injective linear map from any subspace, on which the form may be degenerate, that preserves the forms extends to a linear symplectomorphism, Witt's extension theorem for real symplectic vector spaces (Artin, *Geometric Algebra*, Thm 3.9; McDuff–Salamon, §2.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: every regular Lindelöf space is paracompact, with no Hausdorff assumption (Munkres, *Topology*, Thm 41.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a regular local ring whose support has the dimension of the ring, a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module, is free (Stacks Project, Lemma 10.106.6, Tag 00NT); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for an order O with conductor 𝔣 in a number field K, #Pic(O) · [𝓞_Kˣ : Oˣ] · #(O/𝔣)ˣ = h_K · #(𝓞_K/𝔣)ˣ, the class number formula for orders (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §12, Thm (12.12)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: on the phase space V × V of a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the standard symplectic form, every component of the Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector A = ‖p‖²q − ⟪q, p⟫p − (mκ/‖q‖)q Poisson-commutes with the Kepler Hamiltonian ‖p‖²/(2m) − κ/‖q‖ away from q = 0, so A is conserved (Goldstein–Poole–Safko, *Classical Mechanics*, §3.9); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: for M free over a commutative ring with a basis of at least two vectors and A = Sym M, so that Proj A is projective space, the forms of degree j ≥ 0 are identified with the global sections Γ(Proj A, 𝒪(j)) by r ↦ r/1 (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Prop. II.5.13, Thm III.5.1(a)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: over any commutative ring k and in every degree n, the Pontryagin product gives a linear isomorphism ⋀ⁿH₁(T; k) ≅ Hₙ(T; k) for a torus T = (S¹)^ι, ι finite: the homology of a torus is the exterior algebra on its first homology (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §3.C); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for an elliptic curve E over ℚ, as a statement with nothing proved: for every analytic continuation of L(E, s) to a connected open set containing 1, its order of vanishing at 1 is the rank of E(ℚ) and, when Sha is finite, its leading Taylor coefficient there is Ω·Reg·#Sha·∏c_p/#E(ℚ)_tors² (Silverman, AEC, App. C §16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the blowup Bl_I X of a scheme X along an ideal sheaf I, the relative Proj of the Rees algebra ⊕ₙ Iⁿ, the textbook definition (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.7; Stacks Project, Tag 01OF); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the Chow group CH_k(X) of a locally Noetherian scheme X, its k-cycles modulo rational equivalence, which is generated by locally finite sums of pushforwards of the cycles div(r) on integral closed subschemes of dimension k + 1 (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, §1.3; Stacks Project, Tag 02RV, Def. 42.19.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the Hodge star of an oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension m = k + l, a linear map from smooth real k-forms to smooth l-forms with α ∧ ⋆β = ⟨α, β⟩ vol and ⋆⋆ = (−1)^{kl} (Warner, *Foundations of Differentiable Manifolds and Lie Groups*, §6.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the Stiefel manifold V_k(E), the orthonormal k-frames of a real inner product space E, which for finite-dimensional E is a compact smooth manifold of dimension k·dim E − (k+1 choose 2) (Milnor–Stasheff, *Characteristic Classes*, Ch. 5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a graph of groups over a Serre graph: a group for each vertex, a group for each geometric edge, shared by a dart and its reverse, and an injective homomorphism from each edge group into the group at the dart's target, Serre's definition (Serre, *Trees*, I §4.4, Def. 8); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a limit group, a group with a finite generating tuple whose marking is a limit, in the space of marked groups, of markings of free groups, which does not depend on the tuple (Champetier–Guirardel, *Limit groups as limits of free groups*, Israel J. Math. 146 (2005), Defs 2.1 and 2.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: pseudo-reductivity of an affine group of finite type over a field k, given by its commutative Hopf algebra: smooth, geometrically connected, and with trivial k-unipotent radical (Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, Def. 1.1.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a linear map of modules over a commutative ring is a pseudo-isomorphism when its kernel and cokernel are pseudo-null, finitely generated with zero localization at every prime of height at most one (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, (5.1.5)–(5.1.7); Washington, *Cyclotomic Fields*, §13.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the absolute derived category of curved DG right modules, the Verdier quotient of the curved homotopy category by the absolutely acyclic objects (Positselski, *Differential graded Koszul duality: an introductory survey*, BLMS 55 (2023), §7.6, Defs 7.4–7.6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: the (p, q) torus knot for coprime integers p, q, the smooth embedding z ↦ (zᵖ, z^q)/√2 of the circle into the unit sphere S³ ⊂ ℂ², on the Clifford torus; which torus knots are knotted is not formalised (Rolfsen, *Knots and Links*, Ch. 3 §C); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: an explicit model of the Whitehead link, the smooth two-component link in S³ ⊂ ℂ² formed by the unknot w = 0 and the Whitehead curve, whose annulus diagram has exactly the two clasp crossings; its identification with the link 5²₁ of the tables is not formalised (Rolfsen, *Knots and Links*, Appendix C, 5²₁); compared in Voyager's full-statement test. (Reasons transcribed from Voyager's run notes; the line it posted had none.)

Correctly stated: a real one-form α on a manifold is a contact form when at every point α_x is nonzero and dα_x is nondegenerate on ker α_x; its equivalence with α ∧ (dα)ⁿ ≠ 0 is not yet proved (Geiges, *An Introduction to Contact Topology*, §§1.1, 2.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
